{{Short description|none}} {{for|related races|2026 United States Senate elections}} {{Use American English|date=January 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2025}} {{Infobox election | election_name = 2026 United States Senate election in New Mexico | country = New Mexico | type = presidential | ongoing = yes | election_date = November 3, 2026 | previous_election = 2020 United States Senate election in New Mexico | previous_year = 2020 | next_election = 2032 United States Senate election in New Mexico | next_year = 2032 | image_size = | image1 = Ben Ray Luján, official portrait (119th Congress) (cropped)1.jpg | nominee1 = [[Ben Ray Luján]] | party1 = Democratic Party (United States) | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | image2 = 3x4.svg | nominee2 = Larry Marker | party2 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | map_image = | map_size = | map_caption = | title = U.S. senator | before_election = [[Ben Ray Luján]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = | after_party = }} {{Elections in New Mexico}} The '''2026 United States Senate election in New Mexico''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[New Mexico]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Ben Ray Luján]] is seeking a second term. He is being challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former oil and gas operator Larry Marker. [[Primary election]]s were held on June 2. Luján won the Democratic nomination with 83.7% of the vote against minimal opposition. After no Republicans qualified for the primary ballot, Marker was nominated as a write-in candidate. Republicans have not won a Senate election in New Mexico since [[2002 United States Senate election in New Mexico|2002]]. == Democratic primary == [[Ben Ray Luján]], a member of the Luján political family, was elected in [[2020 United States Senate election in New Mexico|2020]] after serving as the representative for the [[New Mexico's 3rd congressional district|3rd congressional district]] from 2009 until 2021.{{Cite web |last=Yachnin |first=Jennifer |date=2015-06-26 |title=In New Mexico, it's good to be a Luján |url=https://www.eenews.net/articles/in-new-mexico-its-good-to-be-a-lujan/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=E&E News by POLITICO |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |title=LUJÁN, Ben Ray {{!}} US House of Representatives: History, Art & Archives |url=https://history.house.gov/People/Listing/L/LUJAN,-Ben-Ray-(L000570)/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=history.house.gov |language=en}} During his tenure in the Senate, Luján has been an outspoken critic of [[Donald Trump]],{{Cite web |title=New Mexico congressional delegation lambasts Trump's threats against Iran • Source New Mexico |url=https://sourcenm.com/briefs/new-mexico-congressional-delegation-members-lambast-trumps-threats-against-iran/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Source New Mexico |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Pat |date=2026-01-26 |title=New Mexico's Heinrich, Luján pledge 'NO' votes on ICE funding, risking partial shutdown |url=https://nmpoliticalreport.com/2026/01/26/new-mexicos-heinrich-lujan-pledge-no-votes-on-ice-funding-risking-partial-shutdown/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=New Mexico Political Report |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Patrick |date=2026-02-25 |title=NM Democrat says President Trump was "lying to the American people" in State of the Union |url=https://www.ksfr.org/government/2026-02-25/nm-democrat-says-president-trump-was-lying-to-the-american-people-in-state-of-the-union |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=KSFR |language=en}} having voted in line with Trump's stated position only 5% of the time.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-03-07 |title=How often do New Mexico's Senators and Reps vote with Trump? A new report tallies the results. |url=https://nmpoliticalreport.com/2026/03/07/how-often-do-new-mexicos-senators-and-reps-vote-with-trump-a-new-report-tallies-the-results/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=New Mexico Political Report |language=en-US}} Luján was widely considered the favorite in the primary election.{{Cite web |last=Coleman |first=J. Miles |date=2026-02-20 |title=Come On and Take a Free Ride: Looking Back at “Uncontested” Senate Races |url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/come-on-and-take-a-free-ride-looking-back-at-uncontested-senate-races/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Sabato's Crystal Ball |language=en-US}} Luján's sole opponent in the primary is Matt Dodson, a [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] veteran from [[Farmington, New Mexico|Farmington]].{{Cite web |last=Towne |first=Robert |date=2026-02-17 |title=No Republican will challenge US Sen. Ben Ray Luján for reelection |url=https://www.kob.com/news/top-news/no-republican-will-challenge-senator-ben-ray-lujan-for-reelection/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=KOB.com |language=en-US}} A self-described [[Democratic socialism|democratic socialist]], Dodson had previously ran unsuccessfully for local and state offices. Originally failing to achieve the 20% threshold of votes in the Democratic Party convention, he qualified for the ballot through signature collection.{{Cite web |last=Bowling |first=Joshua |date=2026-03-25 |title=NM election officials qualify most statewide candidates for June 2 primary ballot • Source New Mexico |url=https://sourcenm.com/2026/03/25/nm-election-officials-qualify-most-statewide-candidates-for-june-primary-ballot/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Source New Mexico |language=en-US}} Dodson is currently suspended from the state Democratic Party, and had previously accused [[San Juan County, New Mexico|San Juan County]] party chair Mary Schildmeyer of embezzling funds. He denied the allegations, and charges were dropped due to lack of evidence.{{Cite web |last=Bowling |first=Joshua |last2=Lohmann |first2=Patrick |last3=Prokop |first3=Danielle |date=2026-04-03
